newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Shell unit eyes investment in Serbia LPG plants.
newsitem.headline: Shell unit eyes investment in Serbia LPG plants.

text.p: Butagaz International B.V. (BIBV), a member of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, this week discussed investment in the Serbian gas sector with NIS Serbian Oil Industry, a senior BIBV official said on Friday.

"We had a more technical discussion on possibility for investment. There is willingness to cooperate with Shell and we see that as a positive approach for investment," BIBV International Development Manager Jean-Claude Dejouhanet told Reuters.
Ending his visit to LPG (liquified petroleum gas) plants in Serbia, Dejouhanet said LPG was only one of the segments in which Shell initially wanted to invest in Serbia.

"There is a clear need for investment. Standards (in Serbia) are still a bit behind what is a normal Shell standard but we are very impressed with the quality of people which is the more important asset than equipment itself," he said.
Serbia has seven LPG production plants, most of which operate with outdated, in some cases 25 year-old equipment.

BIBV plans to acquire a majority stake in those plants, upgrading them and developing LPG distribution with a possible door-to-door delivery, a source close to negotiations said, speaking under condition of anonymity.
Dejouhanet declined to detail the size of the planned investment, but local sources spoke of several tens of million of dollars.
"The size of the initial investment is difficult to give at this stage. We have not done any technical surveys, we have just visited one of the facilities...," he said.

Before making any final decisions, Butagaz legal experts will scrutinize the new privatisation law and a series of laws regulating foreign investment. The company was also looking into the country's and the industry's growth potential.
"Serbia was consuming 130,000 tonnes of LPG before the war but...it can consume between 250,000 and 350,000 tonnes of LPG within less than two years," Dejouhanet said.
Butagaz officials saw Serbia visibly reopening its economy to the world and saw investment possible for the Shell Group.
A senior Shell official is expected to arrive in Belgrade late next week to discuss further the company's engagement in Serbia.

"Within several days the coordinator for oil products of Shell will come and this is a step forward for a more global investment and interesting involvement," Dejouhanet said. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
